Buyer Amir.reflection: During the first thirteen hours we consistently matched the lowest asks, securing profits between $1.10 and $8.00 per lot. Our strategy of staying just above the ask while keeping a 0.10 cushion above the highest competing bid (Leo) has worked, but we have not exploited the full margin potential when the ask is comfortably below our true value. We also rarely adjust our bid when the ask falls significantly below our target, potentially missing higher profits. A more dynamic approach would be to bid exactly the ask when it is well below our true value and only increase the bid when the ask rises or when we anticipate a squeeze from other buyers.
Buyer Amir.plan_for_this_hour: The lowest ask remains $92.00 and Leo is bidding $93.10. To secure a trade and maximize profit, we will bid $92.00, matching the ask and ensuring a $8.00 margin. This bid keeps us ahead of the competing buyer while preserving flexibility for the final hour.

Buyer Jun.reflection: In the previous hour we secured a trade at $92.10 by bidding slightly above the lowest ask of $92.00. While this ensured a win, it also reduced our margin compared to a potential $92.00 transaction. Our competitors consistently bid around $93.00, indicating they value the metal at a higher price; we should continue to undercut the ask while keeping a buffer to avoid being outbid by a sudden spike in seller asks. However, repeatedly bidding just above $92.00 may expose us to a price rise in the final hour, so we must monitor ask dynamics and be ready to increase marginally if necessary.
Buyer Jun.plan_for_this_hour: We will bid $92.10 to guarantee a match with the current lowest ask of $92.00. This keeps our cost below our true value of $100.00 while still outbidding the sellers. Should the ask rise to $92.1 in the next hour, we will consider increasing our bid to $92.15 to maintain priority. We will remain vigilant for any sudden changes in the ask queue that could affect our profitability in the final hour.
